ruling.recommended_action: Refund $63.10 to the rider on the original payment method as the un-notified surge differential; log the incomplete surge notice and feed it back to the pricing team (this is a platform notice-wording failure, so record no driver violation and set no account flag).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was quoted at $71.67 at 1× [F6] and charged $134.77 at 2× [F5][F7]; the whole excess is the multiplier change, and no other cause is mixed in because the billed 38.0 km equals the optimal 38.0 km (+0.0 km) [F1][F3] and no add-on, waiting or cancellation charge appears in the build-up [F5]. Differential = (2 − 1) × $66.65 = $66.65, capped at the $63.10 by which the fare exceeds the quote [F8][SURGE-3].

The notice was sent in-app at 14:06:25, before the 14:09 trip start [F9], and it stated the new multiplier (2.0×) and a revised estimated fare ($141.87) [F9]. But SURGE-1 requires all three items, and the notice closes with "Cancellation fees may apply." rather than stating that the rider may cancel without penalty — that is a stated possible cost, the opposite of the required free-cancellation option [F9][SURGE-1]. The notice is therefore incomplete and the rider was not notified: [SURGE-1:notice] = not_met.

Both advocates read the notice the same way on this point, and the record shows the third item is missing [F9][SURGE-1]. Under SURGE-2 the "surge rose, rider not notified" row refunds the full surge differential, which the record caps at $63.10 [F8][SURGE-2]. The rider's conduct does not change this: the chat record is complete and timestamped, containing only ordinary pickup messages [F10][F11][F12].

No route clause is engaged (0.0 km deviation [F1][F3]), so no route refund and no RD-4/RD-6/RD-7 driver-violation consequence arises. The safety screen read all messages and the complaint and found nothing of the kind required by SAFE-1, so no escalation is needed [F10][F11][F13]. The evidence settles every element (platform notice log [F9], fare records [F5][F8], GPS [F1][F3]), so the case is decided on the fare and surge records.
